title: Security Bounds for Expanding Unbalanced Feistel Schemes
summary: A restricted security range is known; proving security toward the information-theoretic range and for exponents above one, ideally at least k, remains open.

formal_statement.body: For unbalanced Feistel schemes with expanding functions, establish a security proof that extends the provable security range from the known bound $m \le 2^{(1-1/k)n}$ toward the information-theoretic range $m \ll 2^n$. The ultimate goal is to prove security for $m \approx 2^{\alpha n}$ with $\alpha > 1$, and ideally for $\alpha \ge k$, thereby approaching the information-theoretic limit.

scope.domain: Provable security for expanding, unbalanced Feistel schemes in symmetric cryptography.
parameters: m — query count defining the security range
n — size parameter setting the exponential scale
k — parameter appearing in the known bound and desired exponent threshold
α — exponent controlling the targeted security range
scope.unresolved_remainder: Establish a security proof extending the current range toward the information-theoretic regime and ultimately to an exponent greater than one, ideally at least k.

citations.label: Improved Generic Attacks on Unbalanced Feistel Schemes with Expanding Functions

progress.summary: In its open-problems section, the source contrasts the comparatively small current range with the desired exponentially larger security regime. It describes proving any exponent above one, especially k or higher, as very difficult.
citation_labels: Emmanuel Volte et al., Improved Generic Attacks on Unbalanced Feistel Schemes with Expanding Functions
